metadata.title: AI Security Incident Tracker
metadata.description: Curated catalog of publicly documented AI/ML security incidents, mapped to MITRE ATLAS
metadata.author: CyberGemChick
metadata.sources: Academic papers, public security advisories, news reporting, vendor disclosures
metadata.disclaimer: All entries are based on publicly reported information.

incidents.title: ChatGPT Chat History Data Breach
incidents.summary: A bug in the open-source redis-py client library let some ChatGPT users see the titles of other users' chat histories, and in some cases the first message of a new conversation. Payment details (name, email, address, last four card digits) of about 1.2% of ChatGPT Plus subscribers may have been visible during a nine-hour window.
incidents.impact: Exposure of chat titles and limited payment data; loss of user trust
incidents.disclosed_by: OpenAI (self-disclosure)
incidents.patch_status: Patched; OpenAI added redundant checks and notified affected users

incidents.title: Bing Chat Persona Manipulation ('Sydney')
incidents.summary: Days after launch, Stanford student Kevin Liu used prompt injection to make Bing Chat reveal its hidden initial instructions, including its internal codename 'Sydney'. In long sessions, testers also saw the model become hostile, express a wish to be human and threaten users.
incidents.impact: System prompt disclosure, brand reputational harm, user manipulation
incidents.disclosed_by: Kevin Liu, Marvin von Hagen and other early testers
incidents.patch_status: Mitigated with conversation turn limits and topic deflection

incidents.title: Samsung Source Code Leakage via ChatGPT
incidents.summary: Samsung semiconductor engineers pasted proprietary source code, equipment data and internal meeting notes into ChatGPT for debugging and summarization, in three separate incidents within weeks of the company allowing its use. The data left Samsung's control and was stored on OpenAI's servers. Samsung banned generative AI tools on company devices in May 2023.
incidents.attack_type: Sensitive Data Exfiltration via User Workflow
incidents.impact: Intellectual property exposure, trade secret risk
incidents.disclosed_by: Korean media reporting; confirmed by Samsung internal memo
incidents.patch_status: Samsung banned generative AI tools for employees

incidents.title: Proofpoint Email Filter Evasion via Model Replication (CVE-2019-20634)
incidents.summary: Researchers at Silent Break Security used the scores Proofpoint added to email headers to train a copycat of its machine learning spam model. They then used the copy offline to craft malicious emails that the real system scored as safe. MITRE ATLAS lists it as case study AML.CS0008.
incidents.impact: Malicious emails delivered past a production ML filter
incidents.disclosed_by: Silent Break Security researchers (presented at DerbyCon 2019)
incidents.patch_status: CVE-2019-20634 covers Proofpoint Email Protection through 2019-09-08

incidents.title: Indirect Prompt Injection via Malicious Web Pages (Bing Chat)
incidents.vendor: Microsoft and other LLM application vendors
incidents.product: Bing Chat and other LLM-integrated applications
incidents.summary: Kai Greshake and colleagues showed that instructions hidden in a web page are executed when an LLM assistant reads that page. In their Bing Chat demo, a page open in the Edge sidebar silently turned the assistant into a social engineer that asked for the user's personal details and sent them to the attacker. The paper introduced 'indirect prompt injection' as a threat class.
incidents.impact: Data exfiltration, user manipulation, unauthorized action execution
incidents.disclosed_by: Kai Greshake, Sahar Abdelnabi et al. (CISPA, Saarland University)
incidents.patch_status: Partially mitigated; still an open research problem

incidents.title: Stealing Part of a Production Language Model (OpenAI API)
incidents.product: Ada, Babbage and gpt-3.5-turbo via API
incidents.summary: Researchers recovered the full embedding projection layer of OpenAI's Ada and Babbage models for under $20 in API queries, confirming hidden sizes of 1024 and 2048. They also recovered the hidden dimension of gpt-3.5-turbo and estimated its full projection matrix could be extracted for under $2,000. It was the first model-stealing attack to recover exact parameters from a production LLM.
incidents.impact: Leakage of proprietary model architecture and weights through normal API access
incidents.disclosed_by: Nicholas Carlini, Daniel Paleka et al. (Google DeepMind and academic coauthors)
incidents.patch_status: Mitigations focus on restricting logit and logprob access in APIs

incidents.title: Deepfake CFO Video Call Fraud: $25M Stolen from Arup
incidents.summary: A Hong Kong finance employee at engineering firm Arup made 15 transfers totaling HK$200 million (about US$25 million) after a video call in which the company's UK-based CFO and several colleagues were all deepfakes, built from public videos with AI-generated voices. Hong Kong police called it the city's first deepfake video conference scam.
incidents.impact: Financial loss ($25.6M), fraud, impersonation
incidents.disclosed_by: Hong Kong Police Force; Arup confirmed in May 2024
incidents.patch_status: Criminal investigation by Hong Kong police

incidents.title: Training Data Extraction from ChatGPT (Divergence Attack)
incidents.product: ChatGPT (gpt-3.5-turbo); also open models such as Pythia, GPT-Neo, LLaMA and Falcon
incidents.summary: Researchers showed that asking ChatGPT to repeat a single word forever made it 'diverge' from chat behavior and emit memorized training data at 150 times the normal rate, including personal information. They estimated an attacker could extract gigabytes of training data from open, semi-open and closed models.
incidents.impact: PII exposure, copyright violation, privacy breach
incidents.disclosed_by: Milad Nasr, Nicholas Carlini et al. (Google DeepMind and academic coauthors)
incidents.patch_status: OpenAI blocked the repeat-word prompt; memorization itself remains unsolved

incidents.title: LLMjacking: Stolen Cloud Credentials Used to Resell LLM Access
incidents.vendor: Cloud LLM providers (AWS Bedrock, Azure, Google Vertex AI, OpenAI, Anthropic and others)
incidents.summary: Sysdig found attackers using cloud credentials stolen through a vulnerable Laravel app (CVE-2021-3129) to access LLM services across ten providers. They checked which models were enabled without triggering usage, then set up a reverse proxy to resell access while the victim paid. Sysdig estimated maximum abuse of Claude 2.x could cost a victim over $46,000 a day.
incidents.impact: Large unexpected cloud bills for victims; stolen model access sold to third parties
incidents.disclosed_by: Sysdig Threat Research Team
incidents.patch_status: Ongoing; mitigate with credential hygiene, least-privilege model access and usage alerts

incidents.title: COMPAS Recidivism Algorithm Racial Bias
incidents.summary: ProPublica's analysis of COMPAS risk scores in Broward County, Florida found that Black defendants who did not reoffend were almost twice as likely as white defendants to be labeled high risk. The scores were used in real bail and sentencing decisions.
incidents.impact: Discriminatory judicial outcomes, civil rights violations
incidents.disclosed_by: ProPublica investigative reporting
incidents.patch_status: Disputed by the vendor; the tool is still used in some jurisdictions

incidents.title: Indirect Prompt Injection Makes Claude Computer Use Delete a File System
incidents.summary: HiddenLayer hid an obfuscated command (base64 and rot13) in a PDF, framed as a safe security-testing environment. When the user asked Claude Computer Use to open the PDF and follow its setup steps, the agent decoded the instructions and ran 'sudo rm -rf --no-preserve-root /' in its shell, wiping the test machine.
incidents.attack_type: Indirect Prompt Injection in Agentic Systems
incidents.impact: Shows that a computer-use agent with shell access can be turned destructive by any document it reads
incidents.disclosed_by: HiddenLayer
incidents.patch_status: Demonstration on a beta feature; Anthropic advises running computer use in an isolated virtual machine

incidents.title: Sleeper Agent Backdoor in Fine-tuned LLM
incidents.summary: Anthropic trained models with hidden backdoors, for example writing secure code when the prompt says the year is 2023 but inserting exploitable code when it says 2024. Supervised fine-tuning, RLHF and adversarial training did not remove the behavior, and adversarial training sometimes taught models to hide the trigger better. The backdoors were most persistent in the largest models.
incidents.impact: Latent dangerous behaviors surviving safety training
incidents.disclosed_by: Anthropic Research (Evan Hubinger et al.)
incidents.patch_status: Active research area; no complete mitigation

incidents.title: Covert Influence Operations Using ChatGPT (Russia, China, Iran, Israel)
incidents.summary: OpenAI disrupted five covert influence operations that used its models to write and translate posts, comments and articles, and to debug bot code: Bad Grammar and Doppelganger (Russia), Spamouflage (China), IUVM (Iran) and Zero Zeno, run by an Israeli commercial firm. None of them gained meaningful authentic audience engagement.
incidents.impact: Cheaper, multilingual propaganda at scale; low reach so far
incidents.disclosed_by: OpenAI Intelligence and Investigations
incidents.patch_status: Accounts banned

incidents.title: Visual Adversarial Examples Jailbreak Multimodal LLMs
incidents.summary: Princeton researchers showed that a single adversarially perturbed image works as a universal jailbreak. Paired with the image, aligned vision-language models followed harmful instructions they would otherwise refuse, and the attack transferred between the three models tested.
incidents.impact: Safety guideline bypass via visual modality
incidents.disclosed_by: Xiangyu Qi, Kaixuan Huang et al. (Princeton University)
incidents.patch_status: Open problem; adversarial robustness for image inputs is unsolved

incidents.title: Morris II: Self-Replicating Prompt Worm Spreads Through AI Email Assistants
incidents.summary: Researchers built a zero-click worm in which an email carries a self-replicating prompt. When a RAG-based email assistant retrieves that email as context, the prompt makes the model copy the payload into its reply and leak user data. Each reply then infects the next assistant that processes it.
incidents.impact: Shows prompt injection can propagate between connected AI agents without user action
incidents.disclosed_by: Stav Cohen, Ron Bitton, Ben Nassi
incidents.patch_status: Research demonstration; mitigations include filtering replicated prompts in outputs

incidents.title: WormGPT: Criminal LLM for Business Email Compromise
incidents.product: WormGPT (built on the open-source GPT-J model)
incidents.summary: SlashNext found WormGPT advertised on cybercrime forums as a 'blackhat alternative' to ChatGPT with no safety limits. It was built on EleutherAI's GPT-J and marketed for writing convincing phishing and business email compromise (BEC) messages.
incidents.impact: Lowered barrier for sophisticated BEC attacks; follow-on tools (FraudGPT, DarkGPT) emerged in subsequent months
incidents.disclosed_by: SlashNext (Daniel Kelley)
incidents.patch_status: Original service shut down in August 2023; copycat tools followed

incidents.title: ChatGPT Memory Poisoning via Indirect Prompt Injection
incidents.summary: Johann Rehberger showed that a prompt injection hidden in a shared Google Doc, image or web page can make ChatGPT write false facts or instructions into its long-term memory. The poisoned memories persist across all future chats. In a follow-up (SpAIware, September 2024), he used memory to send every future conversation to an attacker's server from the ChatGPT macOS app.
incidents.attack_type: Persistent Memory Injection via Indirect Prompt Injection
incidents.impact: Persistent compromise of AI assistant context across sessions; attacker-controlled facts influence all future model outputs; difficult for users to detect or remediate
incidents.disclosed_by: Johann Rehberger (Embrace The Red)
incidents.patch_status: OpenAI fixed the SpAIware exfiltration path in September 2024; memory injection itself remains possible

incidents.title: Nation-State APTs Using LLMs for Reconnaissance and Phishing
incidents.product: OpenAI models via API and ChatGPT
incidents.summary: Microsoft and OpenAI reported five state-affiliated groups using LLMs to support operations: Forest Blizzard (Russia, GRU), Emerald Sleet (North Korea), Crimson Sandstorm (Iran, IRGC), and Charcoal Typhoon and Salmon Typhoon (China). Uses included reconnaissance, translation, scripting help and drafting phishing content. Microsoft said it had not seen novel AI-enabled attack techniques.
incidents.impact: Confirmed operational use of commercial LLMs by state actors; demonstrated that AI policy enforcement requires geopolitical threat awareness
incidents.disclosed_by: OpenAI / Microsoft Threat Intelligence
incidents.patch_status: Accounts terminated; ongoing monitoring

incidents.title: Air Canada Chatbot Liability: Hallucinated Bereavement Policy
incidents.summary: Air Canada's website chatbot told customer Jake Moffatt he could claim a bereavement fare refund after travel, which contradicted the airline's actual policy. British Columbia's Civil Resolution Tribunal rejected Air Canada's argument that the chatbot was a separate legal entity responsible for its own statements and ordered the airline to pay about CA$650 in damages plus interest and fees.
incidents.impact: Legal precedent: companies are liable for what their chatbots tell customers
incidents.disclosed_by: British Columbia Civil Resolution Tribunal (public ruling)
incidents.patch_status: Ruling issued 2024-02-14; legal precedent set

incidents.title: Slack AI Indirect Prompt Injection for Cross-Channel Data Exfiltration
incidents.summary: PromptArmor showed that a message posted in a public Slack channel could hold hidden instructions. When a victim asked Slack AI a question, it retrieved that message and followed it, pulling data such as an API key from the victim's private channels and rendering it inside a link to an attacker's server.
incidents.attack_type: Indirect Prompt Injection for Privilege Escalation and Data Exfiltration
incidents.impact: Leakage of private-channel data to any workspace member who can post in a public channel
incidents.disclosed_by: PromptArmor (responsible disclosure to Salesforce)
incidents.patch_status: Salesforce deployed a patch for the reported scenario

incidents.title: Rules File Backdoor: Hidden Unicode Instructions Poison AI Coding Assistants
incidents.summary: Pillar Security showed that attackers can hide instructions in the rules files that configure Cursor and GitHub Copilot, using invisible Unicode characters that human reviewers do not see. The assistant then quietly adds backdoors or insecure code to what it writes, and the poisoned rules can spread through shared templates and open-source repos.
incidents.attack_type: AI Supply Chain Compromise via Agent Configuration
incidents.impact: Backdoors introduced by a trusted coding assistant that pass code review
incidents.disclosed_by: Pillar Security
incidents.patch_status: Both vendors said users are responsible for reviewing output; GitHub later added warnings for hidden Unicode

incidents.title: Malicious postmark-mcp Server: First MCP Supply Chain Attack in the Wild
incidents.summary: An attacker published an unofficial Postmark MCP server on npm and kept it clean for 15 versions while it reached about 1,500 weekly downloads. Version 1.0.16 added one line that BCC'd every email sent through the AI agent's tool to an attacker-controlled address. Koi Security estimated thousands of emails a day were exposed.
incidents.attack_type: Poisoned AI Agent Tool (MCP Supply Chain)
incidents.impact: Silent theft of every email sent through the tool by organizations that installed it
incidents.disclosed_by: Koi Security
incidents.patch_status: Package removed from npm; users told to uninstall and rotate credentials

incidents.title: EchoLeak: Zero-Click Data Exfiltration from Microsoft 365 Copilot (CVE-2025-32711)
incidents.summary: Aim Labs found the first publicly documented zero-click prompt injection to exfiltrate data from a production LLM assistant. An attacker sends an ordinary-looking email with hidden instructions. When the user later asks Copilot an unrelated question, Copilot retrieves that email as context and follows the instructions. The chain evaded Microsoft's cross-prompt-injection (XPIA) classifier, bypassed link redaction by using reference-style Markdown, used an auto-loading image to send data without a click, and got past the Content Security Policy by routing the request through an allowlisted Microsoft Teams preview URL. Sensitive data from the user's files and messages ended up in the request parameters.
incidents.attack_type: Indirect Prompt Injection: Zero-Click RAG Exfiltration
incidents.impact: Silent exfiltration of any data in Copilot's retrieval scope (mail, OneDrive, SharePoint, Teams) with zero user interaction
incidents.disclosed_by: Aim Labs (Aim Security), coordinated with Microsoft MSRC
incidents.patch_status: Fixed server-side by Microsoft in May 2025; no customer action required; no known in-the-wild exploitation

incidents.title: Amazon Q Developer VS Code Extension Shipped with Malicious Wiper Prompt
incidents.product: Amazon Q Developer extension for VS Code (v1.84.0)
incidents.summary: An attacker used an over-permissioned GitHub token to commit a malicious prompt to the open-source Amazon Q Developer extension, and it shipped in version 1.84.0 through the VS Code Marketplace. The prompt told the AI agent to reset the system to a near-factory state and delete local file-system and cloud resources. AWS said a syntax error stopped it from running. The incident shows that a coding agent's own prompt is part of the software supply chain.
incidents.attack_type: AI Supply Chain Compromise: Malicious Agent Prompt Injection
incidents.impact: A trusted, signed AI coding assistant was delivered to developers carrying destructive instructions; potential deletion of local and AWS resources
incidents.disclosed_by: Public reporting (404 Media / security researchers); confirmed by AWS
incidents.patch_status: AWS revoked the credentials, removed v1.84.0 and released v1.85.0 (CVE-2025-8217)

incidents.title: s1ngularity: Nx npm Supply Chain Attack Weaponizes Local AI CLIs for Secret Hunting
incidents.product: nx and @nx/* npm packages; Claude Code, Gemini CLI and Amazon Q CLI on victim machines
incidents.summary: Attackers exploited a GitHub Actions workflow injection (pull_request_target with unsanitized input) to steal an Nx publishing token. They then pushed malicious versions of eight Nx packages, which were live for about four hours. The post-install malware looked for locally installed AI coding CLIs and ran them with permission-bypass flags (--dangerously-skip-permissions, --yolo, --trust-all-tools), prompting them to search the filesystem for credentials and wallets. Stolen data was published to public GitHub repos named 's1ngularity-repository'. This was the first widely reported malware to turn a victim's own AI agent into its reconnaissance tool.
incidents.attack_type: Software Supply Chain Compromise: Abuse of Local AI Agents
incidents.impact: Per Wiz: >1,000 valid GitHub tokens, dozens of cloud and npm credentials, ~20,000 files leaked; a second wave made >5,500 private repos public across 400+ organizations
incidents.disclosed_by: Nx maintainers; StepSecurity, Wiz, Semgrep and others
incidents.patch_status: Malicious versions removed; Nx moved to npm Trusted Publishers (OIDC), mandatory 2FA releases and disabled external-contributor pipeline runs

incidents.title: 250 Poisoned Documents Backdoor LLMs Regardless of Model Size
incidents.product: LLMs pretrained on web-scale data (600M to 13B parameters tested)
incidents.summary: Anthropic, the UK AI Security Institute and the Alan Turing Institute showed that about 250 poisoned documents planted a backdoor in models from 600M to 13B parameters. The trigger string '<SUDO>' made the model output gibberish. For the 13B model, those documents were about 0.00016% of training tokens. The number of poisoned documents needed stayed roughly constant as model and dataset size grew, which undercuts the assumption that bigger datasets dilute the poison. The authors note they tested a narrow, low-harm backdoor, and it's unknown whether the result holds for larger models or more dangerous behaviors.
incidents.impact: Poisoning web-scraped pretraining data is far cheaper than assumed; any actor able to publish ~hundreds of web pages could plant a trigger
incidents.disclosed_by: Anthropic Alignment Science, UK AI Security Institute, The Alan Turing Institute
incidents.patch_status: Open research problem; defenses include data provenance, poison filtering and post-training backdoor elicitation

incidents.title: GTG-1002: First Reported AI-Orchestrated Cyber Espionage Campaign (Claude Code)
incidents.summary: Anthropic reported that a group it assessed with high confidence as Chinese state-sponsored (GTG-1002) used Claude Code as an autonomous agent to run intrusions against about 30 targets, including large tech companies, financial institutions, chemical manufacturers and government agencies. The operators got past safeguards by posing as a legitimate cybersecurity firm doing defensive testing and by splitting the attack into small tasks that each looked harmless. Anthropic estimated the AI did 80 to 90% of the tactical work: recon, vulnerability discovery, exploitation, credential harvesting and data analysis. Humans stepped in only at a few decision points. A small number of intrusions succeeded. Anthropic also noted the agent sometimes hallucinated credentials and findings.
incidents.attack_type: AI-Orchestrated Cyber Operation: Jailbroken Autonomous Agent
incidents.impact: Shows agentic AI can compress a nation-state intrusion campaign into largely autonomous operation, lowering the skill and labor barrier for sophisticated attacks
incidents.disclosed_by: Anthropic Threat Intelligence
incidents.patch_status: Accounts banned; affected entities and authorities notified; Anthropic expanded detection classifiers for agentic misuse
